items.title: 67251_Chuck Green oral history interview
items.q: With the Step Brothers -- that's what he done it with.

ctx.x: Yeah, that's it. That's how you would come out of a hand stand. He did it in one of the east side -- I think it was the East Side Kids movie -- the Bowery Boys, something you know. With the Step Brothers -- that's what he done it with. He was a loader, you know. They had went to some stock room, you know, they had loaded the truck, you know, and they'd be tap dancing. They was doing the Step Brothers dance and while loading these properties on to this truck. And each one of them would do some kind of a tap step…

items.title: 67251_Chuck Green oral history interview
items.q: We worked in there with Buck and Bubbles. I danced with these roller skates on

ctx.x: And was he giving you sort of pointers, in terms of acrobatic tap?

Yeah. Well, see, I was very proud of the handspring, see, and I was in the process of teaching myself how to tap dance with roller skates on. A few times there we worked -- they had a theater there where the Uris is. It was called the Capitol Theater. We worked in there with Buck and Bubbles. I danced with these roller skates on

and I had a little trick that I did where I'd inject the handspring with the roller skates on, and come down with the music, in time with the music, you see? And I must have exagerrated it in some way, because I overdid the handspring and come down, instead of landing on the skates I landed on the skates, but I had to go down and catch myself with my hands, like that, you see, over near the orchestra. It was the thing to -- like you're playing with the musicians, you see, do you know, like that, you know.…

items.title: 67251_Chuck Green oral history interview
items.q: And he started to training Chuckles and I, you know, and he was -- in other words, they were trying to outdo each other... Chuckles and I -- we were getting all these rewards of these teachings, you see, about how to perform and entertain an audience.

ctx.x: Yeah, right, yeah. So then I tried to show this step to Chuckles, you see. I says, now, J. D. -- Slim, see -- and we was having fun with it, and we was telling him about what a nice man Mr. Buddy Bradley was, you know, and he told us where he would be over in New York City, said he would be at the Benepeer Studios down on 46th Street.

And that's the first time I knew that streets had names after numbers, you know, like 46th Street, you know, like between Broadway and Eighth Avenue, you know, and, well, I was fascinated by it. I wanted to go to New York City.

items.title: 67251_Chuck Green oral history interview
items.q: he liked to see me dance like John Bubbles at that time, because John Bubbles was known as a great jazz singer.

ctx.x: What sort of things did you cut away from it? What sort of mistakes were you making?

Well, we weren't actually making mistakes. The idea was they loved improvement, you see, and it was either Nat Nazarra or John Bubbles thought that it would be better for us, it would be more of an improvement for to improve on there to take that away and don't do it first, do it second, and like that, whatever they had us doing. So --
Were there things that you created on your own?
